material_sources.title: Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (2024), 33, pp. 16–31
material_sources.relationship_to_claim: States every q-step graphon is forced by graphs on at most 4q^2-q vertices (14 for q=2; 2q+1 only under distinct block degrees), a strictly weaker uniform bound than the headline m=4 with its explicit six-graph set and exact inversion formulas.

material_sources.title: The Graph Pencil Method:
material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Shows degree-separated K-block SBMs are determined by finitely many star/bistar densities for inference, but explicitly excludes the regular equal-degree slice that the headline resolves via triangle plus diamond identities, and gives no uniform 4-vertex forcing set.

material_sources.title: Random graphs and network statistics
material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Gives consistent statistical estimation of a large sparse doubly-stochastic 2-community block model from empirical star covering densities; its conclusion is asymptotic consistency of estimators, not exact determination of every 2-block graphon by six small densities.

material_sources.title: arXiv:1302.2684v4  [cs.LG]  24 Oct 2013
material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Proves MMSB/SBM identifiability from third-order 3-star tensor moments under full-rank connectivity and size conditions; a statistical tensor-decomposition result, not exact uniform forcing by connected graphs on at most 4 vertices for all parameters.

material_sources.title: Graph limits and their applications in extremal combinatorics
material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Survey restatement of the Lovasz-Sos theorem that every step graphon is finitely forcible by some unspecified finite family; it supplies no uniform m=4 bound, no six-graph list, and no P4/triangle/diamond inversion, so it is strictly weaker than the headline.
